description.narrative: Souphanouvong University (SU) plays a pivotal role in the IP3 project as a leading academic institution in northern Laos with deep expertise in the Mekong region's geographical and social context. The university contributes specialized knowledge in environmental science, water management, and Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), leveraging its team of researchers, professors, and students who possess strong understanding of local participatory processes. This enables effective engagement with vulnerable groups, including women, youth, and persons with disabilities, ensuring inclusive and well-coordinated project implementation. Oxfam provides critical support to SU through financial backing for operations and GEDSI initiatives, technical training in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL), Theory of Change (ToC), and climate adaptation, as well as capacity-building workshops and collaborative research. Additionally, Oxfam assists in project management and coordination by enhancing communication, scaling up results, and linking local data to global systems. SU adds unique value to the partnership through its credibility as an academic institution with robust data verification mechanisms, unparalleled access to remote communities, and the ability to foster collaboration between academia, policymakers, and local stakeholders. By involving students and researchers in fieldwork, SU generateshigh-quality evidence grounded in local experience while its coordinators serve as vital connectors between Oxfam, communities, anddecision-makers. With a proven track record in Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM), climate adaptation, and social inclusion, SU excels in evidence-based research, participatory training, and financial management—adhering to international reporting standards and maintaining transparent procurement processes. However, capacity-building needs remain, particularly in advancing MEAL systems, digital storytelling, and scaling up project impacts through improved knowledge-sharing and adaptive management. Overall, SU’s multidimensional partnership with Oxfam strengthens the sustainability and effectiveness of the IP3 project, driving data-informed policy changes and transformative outcomes in the Mekong region.

participating-org.narrative:
Souphanouvong University (SU) is a university in Luang Prabang, the old capital of Laos and its fourth largest city. It is one of five national universities in the country. It was established in accordance with the Prime Minister Decree, No 169/PM, dated4 November 2003, and inaugurated on the following day. The University is named after Prince Souphanouvong, who was the first President of theDemocratic People's Republic of Laos.[1]
According to the Prime Minister Decree on the Organization and Activities of Souphanouvong University, No 099/PM, dated 3 April 2009, SU is a public national educational and cultural institution under the Ministry of Education. The University carries out the educational functions of preparing specialists, researchers and multidisciplinary scientific scholars; organizing scientific research; protecting and promoting Lao’s unique national and multiethnic arts and culture; and delivering academic services to society.
